title: Experimental Topics
description: Selected topics.

title: Special Study
description: Individual study.

title: Topics in Educational Leadership
description: Selected problems in educational leadership.

title: Organizational and Systems Leadership
description: Educational administration and leadership as a profession. Related organizational concepts and management theories. Principles and competencies for leadership and administrative practice as each relates to the aspiring school administrator.

title: Visionary Leadership
description: Concepts and techniques of leadership, analysis of factors and practice in procedures of individual and group leadership as applied to preK-12 educational environments.

title: Leading Equity in Schools
description: Supporting equity for students in preK-12 schools through leadership roles. Common biases and inequities that affect students based on ability, gender, national origin, race, religion, and sexual orientation. Systems design for reducing inequities for all learners.

title: Leading Teams to Use Evidence-Based Practices
description: Evaluation of sources of evidence, identification of best practices, and needs assessment. Accessing research to improve uses of evidence-based practices and implementation science.

title: Mentoring, Coaching, and Collaboration
description: Leadership and institutional improvement. Adult learning theory models and methods to improve collaboration between communities, families, and schools.

title: Organizational Engagement
description: Invitational education and implementation science. Designing professional learning opportunities and leading communities for improvement and increased engagement.

title: School Improvement Leadership
description: Analyzing data to identify opportunities for school improvement. Appropriate and effective school improvement theories and strategies. Communication skills and leading others in improvement and monitoring of these efforts.

title: Community Leadership
description: Increasing family and community involvement in schools. Improving student achievement through using educational leadership strategies and resources.

title: Professional Learning and Growth Leadership
description: Model professional growth development. Principles of adult learning; identify and facilitate appropriate professional growth opportunities for staff. Collaboration with others to achieve mission of improving teaching and learning.

title: Seminar in Instructional Leadership
description: Improvement of instruction through application of principles and practices in assessment of teaching competency; development of teaching profiles; leadership skills in working with teachers to improve performance.

title: Communication, Problem Solving, and Decision Making in PK12
description: Educational leadership principles and practices for communication, problem solving, and decision making in preK-12 schools and educational organizations.

title: Field Experience in Educational Leadership
description: Supervised field experience in schools or other educational settings. Monthly sessions with university faculty. Application to take this course must be made during preceding semester.

title: Seminar in PreK-12 Educational Administration
description: Educational administration in preK-12 schools and school districts. Field experience when appropriate.

title: PK-12 Needs Assessment & Program Evaluation I
description: Needs assessment and program evaluation to inform practice and amplify student impact. Students establish project focus and frame inquiry work for the EDL 690-691-692 sequence. Review extant data, understand opportunity and develop inquiry plan to guide data collection effort.

title: PK-12 Needs Assessment & Program Evaluation II
description: Implementation of PK-12 needs assessment or program evaluation inquiry plans developed in

title: Data for PK-12 Program Design, Appreciation, and Improvement
description: Analysis and reporting of needs assessment and program evaluation findings. Examine qualitative and quantitative data as framed by inquiry plan. Author and present findings, including strengths, recommendations for improvement, and implications for leaders. Reflect on inquiry process for future application.

title: Advanced Topics in Educational Leadership
description: Intensive study in specific areas of educational leadership.

title: Educational Law and Finance
description: Legal and financial aspects of educational administration including implications for policy formulation in the areas of personnel, instruction, and resource management.

title: Human Resource Development in PreK-12 Educational Organizations
description: Human resource management in preK-12 educational administration including selection and evaluation of staff, contract management, and staff development. Personnel managerial styles, staff leadership, and motivation techniques as to morale and productivity. Analysis of educational personnel systems and employee assistance programs.

title: Governance and Policy Development in PreK-12 Learning Organizations
description: Development of preK-12 educational policy and impact of politics in governance and administration; control functions of federal, state, and local agencies; influence of lay citizens and special interest groups; roles of judiciary, employee organizations and students.

title: Practicum in PreK-12 Educational Organizations
description: Internship for preK-12 educational administrators. Application to take this course must be made in the preceding semester by preregistration with the credential program coordinator. Released time may be required.

title: Special Study
description: May involve fieldwork.

title: Leadership for Learning
description: Models of curriculum, instruction, and school organization. The leader’s role and responsibility in developing evidence-based decision making cultures that promote student achievement.

title: Seminar in Topics in Educational Leadership
description: Topical issues in field of educational leadership that have broad implications for research and practice in educational leadership.

title: Foundations of PK-12 Research and Evaluation I
description: Foundational knowledge in research and program evaluation. Introduction to qualitative and quantitative methods, including their application to empirical research and program evaluation. Application of skills professionally and to an original research or program evaluation to fulfill doctoral program requirements.

title: Foundations of PK-12 Research and Evaluation II
description: Advanced exploration of research and program evaluation. Qualitative, quantitative, and program evaluation including mixed methods design. Methodology planning, instrument design, data analysis planning. Application of skills professionally and to an original research or program evaluation to fulfill doctoral program requirements.

title: Application of PK-12 Research and Evaluation
description: Continued exploration of research and program evaluation design. Qualitative, quantitative, and program evaluation including mixed methods design. Formulation of an initial research or program evaluation methodology to address a researchable problem or program evaluation.

title: Doctoral Dissertation
description: Preparation of the dissertation for the doctoral degree. Enrollment is required during the term in which the dissertation is approved. No unit credit allowed toward advanced degree.
